title: Associate Director, AMI Curricula
description:
About AbbVie
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/ . Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.
The Associate Director of AMI Curricula is responsible for the development of curricula across Allergan Medical Institute educational programs, primarily new large group programs in-field and in the Training Centers. Main responsibilities include collaboration with key stakeholders (AMI Programs team, Customer Marketing teams, Training Centers team, Design & Internal review team, etc) to develop content to achieve our educational objectives across the HCP learning journey.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following (other duties may be assigned.):
Lead the development of AMI curricula across all large group programming in the AMI Training Centers and in-field programming
Strategic oversight of AMI content and tactics as it relates to large group programs, including: Net new program creation based on Learning Journey, business needs, market demand
Go to market strategy for new programs through Field and digital channels
Strategy for Faculty speaker training and selection, ongoing Faculty training post-launch
Oversight of development of all training materials, videos, slide decks, etc, aligning to brand strategy, KOL review, and adult learning principles
Curricula Lead for all internal Sales communications, including: Liaison between Curricula and Faculty Development team
Coordination of any new initiatives with Commercial Directors
Development of Field Resources (sales aids, targeting tools, etc)
Management of agency partners and content designers to ensure content adheres to creative and curricula briefs, brand guidelines, and MLRC review guidelines
Management of ‘Large Group/Training Center AMI pillar’ team members
Oversight of all workshop and agenda development
Responsible for capturing KOL advisor feedback across all programs
Translating key strategic initiatives into plans and go-to-market tactics for new AMI engagement programs
Coordinating cross-functional internal resources and third parties/vendors for the execution of AMI Engagement initiatives
Building and maintaining strong relationships with KOLs, thought leaders, and other key stakeholders
Coordinating with, and training HCP partners to ensure the execution of successful training programs
Perform other duties as assigned
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent is required.
Minimum of 10 years related experience is preferred.
Experience in curricula development
Experience on product/indication launches
Experience managing a team
Proficient with Microsoft Office, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to communicate clearly and professionally.
Knowledge of FDA and regulatory statutes as applied to Allergan Aesthetics products, with the ability to function in an environment controlled by outside regulatory entities.
Knowledge of procedure training, consultation, business-to business (B2B) and selling skills are desired.
High degree of flexibility in adapting to a rapidly changing environment.
Occasional flexibility in work hours, including weekends, may be required.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
Additional Requirements:
Ability to travel up to 40%. Evenings, overnight, weekends, domestic is required.
Language and Verbal Skills:
Individual must have excellent verbal and written communication skills and a demonstrated ability to communicate clearly and professionally.
Analytical and Reading Skills:
Ability to read, understand and abide by company procedures. Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, draw valid conclusions and report on findings.

title: Associate Director, Chief of Staff – People Experience
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Position Summary
The Associate Director, Chief of Staff – People Experience (PE) serves as a strategic partner and trusted advisor to the PE Leadership Team, driving the execution and acceleration of the People Experience vision. This role is a core member of the PE leadership team, responsible for optimizing the PE organization itself — how it operates, prioritizes, plans, and delivers against its agenda. The Chief of Staff acts as an integrator, communicator, and accelerator, translating PE's vision into tangible outcomes and ensuring the PE team functions at its highest potential.
Note: This role is focused on PE organizational optimization — not broad HR optimization, which is a shared accountability across the entire PE team. The Chief of Staff ensures PE as an organization runs with excellence, coherence, and strategic clarity.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership & Vision Acceleration
Partner with the Head of People Experience and PE leadership to define, refine, and cascade the PE vision and multi-year strategy.
Identify and resolve strategic gaps, dependencies, and opportunities that affect execution of the PE agenda.
Serve as a thought partner to senior PE leaders, bringing an enterprise perspective and anticipating organizational needs before they arise.
Synthesize complex information and distill it into clear, compelling narratives for leadership and stakeholders.
PE Organizational Optimization
Own the continuous improvement of how the PE organization operates — including how the team is structured to deliver, how decisions get made, and how work gets done.
Drive clarity on roles, accountabilities, and interdependencies across PE sub-functions to eliminate duplication and increase team effectiveness.
Identify operational inefficiencies within PE and implement scalable solutions to improve team performance and output quality.
Partner with PE leaders to assess and evolve the operating model as the team's scope and strategy evolve.
Note: Broad HR optimization (e.g., improving HR programs and services for the enterprise) is a shared responsibility across the entire PE team. This role is specifically accountable for optimizing the PE organization itself.
Prioritization & Portfolio Management
Lead and manage the PE Leadership Team's portfolio of strategic initiatives, ensuring alignment to top priorities and business outcomes.
Drive rigorous prioritization frameworks to focus PE resources on the highest-value work.
Track progress against strategic goals and OKRs; escalate risks and recommend course corrections as needed.
Partner with Finance and HR Operations on PE resource planning and investment decisions.
Rhythms of Business & Operating Model
Design, own, and continuously improve the rhythms of business for the PE organization, including leadership team meetings, planning cycles, business reviews, and all-hands communications.
Prepare and curate agendas, pre-reads, and follow-up actions for PE Leadership Team meetings to ensure productive, outcome-oriented sessions.
Coordinate and manage annual and quarterly planning processes, connecting PE plans to broader AbbVie enterprise cycles.
Build and maintain a PE operating calendar that ensures key milestones, deliverables, and decisions are managed proactively.
Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement
Serve as a connector across PE sub-functions, breaking down silos and ensuring integrated execution of the PE strategy.
Represent the PE Leadership Team in cross-functional forums, working groups, and enterprise planning processes.
Build strong relationships with key stakeholders across HR, Business HR, Finance, Communications, and other enabling functions.
Communications & Change Enablement
Develop compelling internal communications for the PE organization, including leadership messages, town halls, strategy updates, and culture-building content.
Champion change management best practices to support adoption of new PE programs, processes, and ways of working within the PE team.
Elevate the PE team's visibility and brand across the enterprise through strategic storytelling and engagement.
Team Effectiveness & Culture
Foster a high-performing, inclusive team culture within the PE Leadership Team and broader PE organization.
Lead special projects and initiatives that strengthen PE organizational effectiveness, engagement, and capability building.
Act as a culture carrier for the PE vision — modeling AbbVie's values and the behaviors the PE team aspires to enable.
Required
Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field.
7+ years of progressive experience in HR, strategy, operations, or a related discipline.
Demonstrated experience operating at a senior level and influencing without direct authority.
Proven ability to manage complex, cross-functional initiatives in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Strong executive communication skills — both written and verbal — with the ability to synthesize complexity for senior audiences.
High learning agility, intellectual curiosity, and comfort navigating ambiguity.
Preferred
MBA or advanced degree.
Prior Chief of Staff, HR Strategy, or HR Business Partner experience at a large, matrixed organization.
Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, or life sciences industry.
Familiarity with organizational design, change management, and workforce planning methodologies.
Competencies
Strategic Thinking & Business Acumen
Influence & Stakeholder Management
Executive Presence & Communication
Execution Discipline & Prioritization
Collaboration & Integration
Learning Agility & Innovation Mindset
Inclusive Leadership
Why People Experience at AbbVie
The People Experience team is at the heart of how AbbVie attracts, develops, and retains the world-class talent needed to deliver on its mission. As a member of the PE Leadership Team, the Associate Director, Chief of Staff will have a front-row seat to enterprise-wide transformation — with a unique opportunity to shape how the PE organization operates and delivers its vision for AbbVie's people now and into the future.

title: Director, EEDI Business Lead- Commercial
description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. For more information about AbbVie, please visit us at  www.abbvie.com . Follow @abbvie on  LinkedIn,   Facebook ,  Instagram ,  X  and  YouTube.
Purpose
This role leads the design and execution of Equity, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EEDI) strategies for one of AbbVie's key functions. Reporting to the Director, Programs and Business Partnerships, this individual serves as a strategic driver and takes a hands-on approach — shaping the vision and rolling up their sleeves to make it real. The role partners closely with VP-level leaders, functional EEDI councils, Business HR (BHR), and HR Centers of Excellence (COEs) to deliver measurable business and talent outcomes.
The ideal candidate brings a demonstrated track record of driving organizational impact at scale — someone who combines forward-thinking strategy with a bias for action, and who is equally comfortable setting direction and doing the work. This person operates with both a grounding in proven approaches and a commitment to evolving practices that serve our global, diverse organization.
Responsibilities
Own EEDI functional strategy: Partner with the business to develop the EEDI strategy for assigned function. Lead strategy execution, including roadmap implementation, stakeholder management, communication plans, and achievement of clear measures of success.
Lead and align EEDI councils: Direct the work of EEDI councils by establishing clear goals, aligned priorities, and effective operating models that connect directly to business and EEDI strategy. Facilitate council effectiveness with hands-on engagement through active leadership.
Co-design and manage EEDI programs: Co-design, deliver, and manage EEDI programs that are intentionally inclusive and accessible to all employees. Take ownership of program outcomes, with accountability for adoption and measurable outcomes.
Drive cross-functional alignment: Partner with EEDI leads, BHR and COEs to integrate EEDI principles into foundational people processes and to collaboratively advance new strategies and initiatives — ensuring consistency and coherence across the enterprise.
Embed systemic change in talent processes: Apply change management methodologies to deliver year-over-year progress on key EEDI metrics and overall talent metrics. Ensure aligned and systemic changes across functions, sustained efforts over one-time initiatives.
Serve as a strategic advisor: Advise BHR and COEs on practical, evidence-based ways to embed EEDI into all people and business processes. Provide thought leadership that shapes the HR practices and promotes equitable decision-making — with both global perspective and local sensitivity.
Research and benchmark: Stay up to date on ongoing research and external benchmarking to inform best practices and to identify new opportunities for building a globally inclusive workforce.
Translate data into action: Use AI, workforce data and analytics to identify talent opportunities, assess initiative effectiveness, and establish KPIs that demonstrate measurable business impact. Be a practitioner who understands data and interprets what it means.
Uphold governance standards: Ensure consistent adherence to governance processes and guidelines across all EEDI programming and initiatives.
Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Advanced degree or EEDI Certification preferred.
Minimum 8+ years of related EEDI work experience; 5+ years of leadership or high-level consulting roles.
Experience in translating external and internal trends into innovative practices.
Proven track record of facilitating company-level initiatives with multiple stakeholders.
A deep understanding of how to promote EEDI within a large, complex, multi-national organization.
Experience in senior business partnering and advisory roles; ability to build collaborative, business-focused relationships with senior HR and business leaders.
Strong consulting skills, project planning, management and review, with an ability to roll up sleeves to demonstrate initiative and results-orientation, with a focus on service.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, presentation skills, and facilitation skills.

title: Post-Incident Reviews (PIR) & Service Health Program Engineer, Infrastructure Services
description:
Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.
Infrastructure Services is part of IS&T and the foundation of Apple's global network operations — managing data center equipment and systems to deliver compute, storage, and networking services for teams across Apple, including its internal developer community. From individual facilities to a worldwide network, Infrastructure Services ensures the technology underneath everything works without question
Edge Production Engineering keeps Apple’s edge infrastructure operating reliably and resiliently at massive global scale. Our ecosystem encompasses CDN and high-throughput reverse proxy services, authoritative and recursive DNS, Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB), and distributed Edge Cloud and compute platforms. Together, these systems deliver critical traffic routing, caching, and infrastructure services to hundreds of millions of users worldwide.
When incidents occur across this multifaceted stack, our ability to coordinate effectively, learn quickly, adapt rigorously, and prevent repeat issues is essential.
We are seeking a Post-Incident Reviews (PIR) & Service Health Program Engineer to help coordinate and drive our PIR lifecycle, remediation tracking, and service health governance across Edge Production Engineering.
In this role, your background in incident response and management will be central to your success. You will guide PIR debriefs with structure and neutrality, ask insightful questions to uncover root causes, ensure remediation action items don’t fall through the cracks, and bring a forward-thinking mindset to leverage Generative AI and modern automation to make our incident learning workflows faster, lighter, and more productive for engineers.
Minimum qualifications: 3+ years of experience in Incident Management, Major Incident Management (MIM), Incident Response, or Technical Support Operations.
Demonstrated experience coordinating major incident response, facilitating incident bridge calls, or conducting post-incident reviews/retrospectives.
Hands-on experience managing operational action items, incident remediation tracking, or process governance using ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow, Jira, or equivalent platforms).
Proven track record drafting incident documentation, executive status updates, operational runbooks, or post-incident summaries.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
Preferred qualifications: Strong meeting facilitation and communication skills, with the poise to lead structured, blameless debriefs with senior engineers and leadership.
Familiarity with DNS, CDN, and basic networking principles.
Technical curiosity and literacy: comfortable collaborating with engineering teams in complex infrastructure or cloud environments to translate technical discussions into clear root- cause narratives.
Interest or hands-on experience leveraging Generative AI tools (e.g., LLM prompting, workflow automation, or scripting) to summarize incident data, draft timelines, and streamline program workflows.
Experience defining, modernizing, or standardizing PIR templates, severity guidelines, or service health metrics.
Experience partnering with central incident management organizations or working with automated incident response bots and tooling.

title: RF System Integration Engineer — Cellular Technology
description:
Apple System RF team is looking for an experienced Radio Frequency (RF) System Integration Engineer to lead the development and optimization of RF automation testing systems used across Apple's cellular products. You'll bring deep technical judgment to a high-caliber, global team, driving system architecture decisions and mentoring other engineers while staying hands-on with the hardest RF problems.
You will take a technical leadership role within a hands-on development team, driving engineering rigor, creativity, and innovation across multiple product lines. We're looking for a seasoned engineer who can operate independently in ambiguous problem spaces, define solutions that don't yet exist, and raise the bar for the team around them.
Minimum qualifications: Demonstrated depth in RF fundamentals and communications theory sufficient to independently diagnose novel RF impairments without guidance.
5+ years hands-on experience with RF lab equipment, including having specified or architected test setups, not just operated them.
6+ years professional experience in C/C++ system-level software development, including having designed and shipped non-trivial systems (not just feature work).
Proven experience designing or leading development of RF test automation systems or frameworks, end-to-end.
Working proficiency with data processing/statistical analysis tools (e.g., Python, MATLAB, or equivalent) applied to RF/test data at scale.
Experience operating with significant autonomy on ambiguous, cross-functional technical problems, with a track record other engineers can point to.
Preferred qualifications: Deep experience with current/emerging Cellular standards (LTE, 5G NR, etc.).
Track record designing and shipping RF test solutions/systems from scratch.
Experience mentoring or leading small technical efforts.
Experience using agentic workflows for software development and data processing.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
6+ years of relevant industry experience in RF engineering, test systems, or wireless communications.
Track record of owning complex technical problems end-to-end, from architecture through delivery.
Experience mentoring engineers and influencing technical direction across teams.

title: RF/Analog Mixed Signal Design Engineer
description:
Imagine what you could do here at Apple? Together we could help craft the next generation of the world’s finest devices. Strong track record of delivering silicon IPs with complete architecture, design, verification and validation experience.
Solid understanding/experience in bandgaps, bias, opamps, switched-cap circuits, LDOs, low power oscillators, PLLs, VGAs, feedback and compensation techniques.
In-depth knowledge and analytical understanding of mixed-signal design techniques.
Experience in understanding top level verification methods incorporating block level schematics and behavioral models.
Experience in C/Matlab/VerilogA/Python modeling.
Hands-on experience in using spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, and signal generators to validate analog designs.
Good knowledge of high precision techniques in presence of device mismatch.
Understanding of data converter architectures and design trade-offs.

description:
Imagine what you could do here at Apple! Together we could help craft the next generation of the world’s finest devices. Bring passion and dedication to your career, and there's no telling what you could accomplish. Proficiency in circuit modeling and simulation, including SPICE models and worst-case corner selection.

Experience in SRAM design.
Experience in timing / SDC constraints generation and management.

title: Security Site Reliability Engineer - Apple Service Engineering
description:
People at Apple don't just build products, they craft the kind of experiences that have revolutionized entire industries. The diverse collection of our people and their ideas inspire innovation in everything we do. Imagine what you could do here. Join Apple, and help us leave the world better than we found it. The Apple Service Engineering (ASE) team builds and provides the systems and infrastructure that fuel Apple's services, including iCloud, iTunes, Siri, and Maps. We are the foundation on which Apple's software developers build the products our customers love.
We are looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to join ASE Security SRE, working in close partnership with development teams to operate and mature services spanning identity, token issuance, and access management. These services sit directly in the path of customer-facing flows and carry significant blast radius. This role works day to day with the engineering teams who build these services, sharing ownership of their reliability, operational quality, and on-call.
We are seeking a Site Reliability Engineer to join a team working directly alongside development partners across identity, token issuance, and access management. You will share responsibility for the reliability, operability, and security posture of the services in this area, contributing from design and planning through to production operation and incident response. You will have a seat in planning and design reviews, and be accountable for operational quality alongside the engineers who build the service.
You will help define and drive adoption of sound operational practices, grounded in what actually works for the team and the threat model in front of them. You will bring deep comfort with distributed, stateful systems operating at scale and high availability expectations.

7+ years in a Site Reliability Engineering or infrastructure focused role
Strong working experience in at least one of: Golang or Swift
Deep experience with distributed, stateful systems operating at high scale and high availability
Strong understanding of networking, storage, and performance at scale
Experience running Tier 1 services with 24/7 support expectations
Knowledge of securing APIs, including authentication and authorization mechanisms for RESTful and gRPC APIs
Understanding of authentication protocols such as OAuth and JWT

Experience with authentication, authorization, or cryptographic systems
Strong grasp of SRE principles including monitoring, alerting, error budgets, and fault analysis
Experience partnering directly with product or platform engineering teams on reliability

title: Senior Creative Gameplay Engineer, Apple Arcade
description:
Apple Arcade is redefining the future of games by offering players of all ages a growing collection of award-winning titles with no ads, no in-app purchases, and a commitment to quality, creativity, and fun. At the heart of this vision is Sneaky Sasquatch, one of Arcade’s most beloved originals.
To help define the future for this celebrated game, Apple is building a team to expand the creative boundaries of Sneaky Sasquatch, to imagine and build entirely new adventures, while introducing the magic of shared, connected gameplay.
This is an opportunity to join a focused, creatively-driven team to develop new content and features that will deliver magical experiences to millions of players. You will work directly alongside the original creators, shaping the future of a renowned IP and helping to establish a culture of creative and technical excellence from the ground up.
As a Senior Creative Gameplay Engineer, you will contribute creative vision and technical expertise to the Sneaky Sasquatch team, creating innovative new gameplay experiences for millions of players around the world.
Minimum qualifications: 10+ years of experience in game development, with a portfolio demonstrating exceptional creative and technical ownership on multiple shipped titles. This includes deep expertise in Unity and C#, with proven mastery of building complex gameplay systems from the ground up.
Preferred qualifications: A proven ability to "find the fun" through rapid prototyping and iteration. Your portfolio should show us how you've turned a rough idea into a polished, delightful experience.
A deep understanding of gameplay systems design. You think in terms of scalable frameworks, not just one-off features.
A highly self-directed and resourceful attitude, comfortable navigating the ambiguity of the creative process.
Excellent communication skills and a passion for collaborative, team-oriented problem-solving.
Experience in a "technical design" or similar hybrid role where you were responsible for both the design and implementation of core gameplay.
Experience shipping on Apple platforms (iOS, tvOS, macOS, visionOS).
Deep familiarity with a wide range of game genres, with strong, well-reasoned opinions on game feel, pacing, and player motivation.
A genuine love for Sneaky Sasquatch and a passion for creating heartfelt, player-centered experiences.

title: Senior Rendering Engine Software Engineer
description:
Apple Maps offers a constantly evolving and increasingly detailed 3D world, and our team renders every frame of it. We develop the graphics engine that powers the mapping and navigation experiences across Apple's entire device ecosystem, from Watch to Vision Pro, as well as the Web. We're looking for a Senior Rendering Engine Software Engineer who is excited by the challenge of rendering our planet beautifully and performantly in real time.
We are the Map Display team, and every day our work is used by hundreds of millions of people to explore and navigate the world. We own the 3D visual experience inside Apple Maps and the graphics engine that fuels a thriving ecosystem of first- and third-party applications. You'll work at the intersection of art and engineering, developing novel algorithms, pushing rendering techniques forward, and collaborating with world-class designers and cartographers to make every pixel perfect. Whether it's the 3D imagery and splats of Yosemite National Park, the historical landmarks of Rome, the streets of Paris, or the transit systems of Tokyo, you'll have a hand in how people interact with our world.
Minimum qualifications: BA/BS plus 5 years of hands-on experience building real-time 3D rendering applications
Mastery of writing C++ that is safe, performant, readable, and built to last
Experience with one or more modern graphics APIs (e.g., Metal, Vulkan, Direct3D 12, WebGPU) and shading languages (e.g., MSL, HLSL, GLSL, WGSL)
Ability to use 3D geometry and linear algebra to solve graphics problems
Experience with multi-threaded engine architectures and synchronization
Methodical debugging mindset and tenacious problem-solving instincts
Communication skills to make complex ideas clear to leadership and the collaboration skills to focus teams’ efforts
Deep ownership of the features you ship
Preferred qualifications: Track record of shipping interactive rendering or game engines at scale for mobile platforms such as iOS, Android, or Linux
Experience navigating the entire lifecycle of software development, from whiteboarding designs to shipping quality, optimized code
Proficiency with GPU profiling tools and performance optimization for mobile platforms
Familiarity with AR/VR rendering technologies and the unique challenges of immersive environments

title: Senior Software Engineer, Apple Services Engineering
description:
We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to help develop the next-generation of Apple’s cloud services infrastructure. You will be working on CloudKit, Apple’s foundational privacy-focused database platform, which securely stores users’ data and seamlessly keeps it synchronized across all their Apple devices.
CloudKit manages data at a massive scale! It is a strongly-consistent database of structured data that serves billions of active Apple customers. Considered the bedrock of iCloud, it is purpose built to be performant, highly available, and extremely scalable. CloudKit is a framework designed to the highest standards of user privacy that not only empowers developers to build highly collaborative and secure applications but is also the storage foundation for Apple’s signature cloud experiences, such as Photos, Drive, Notes, Keynote, News, and many third-party applications!
We are a world-class team who has a real passion for engineering and delivering high quality services to Apple’s customers. As a key member of a versatile organization, you will introduce new fundamental capabilities that will help power entirely new applications and scale existing ones.
We are looking for engineers who have exceptional expertise in building fault-tolerant distributed systems. Our engineers demonstrate unique leadership skills and can excel in a complex environment that obsesses about the customer experience.
Minimum qualifications: 7+ years of industry experience developing software in Java, C, or C++
Experience working with distributed NoSQL and relational database technologies
Expertise in synchronous and asynchronous network application I/O frameworks
Expertise in programming in concurrent and multi-threaded environments
Industry experience building and operating large-scale multi-tiered distributed systems
Bachelor’s degree in an engineering-related field or equivalent related experience
Preferred qualifications: Strong background with KV data stores, e.g., FoundationDB, DynamoDB, or Cassandra
Strong fundamentals in storage systems, e.g., schema design, indexes, and transactions
Familiar with high-performance caching mechanisms, e.g., Redis or Memcached
Familiar with event streaming and queueing systems, e.g., Kafka
Experience using AWS, GCP, and cloud-native technologies (Containers, Kubernetes, gRPC)
Experience with TLS, X.509 certificates, or similar security and cryptographic protocols

Your contributions will enable the development of entirely new applications and the scaling of existing ones, such as CloudKit, FaceTime, and PushNotifications, which serve as the foundation for products like iCloud Photos, Drive, and Backup.

title: Sensing FEA Engineer
description:
At Apple, outstanding ideas have a way of becoming phenomenal products, services, and customer experiences very quickly. Bring your passion, dedication and expertise to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. We are seeking a finite element analyst to conduct structural, thermal, and dynamic analysis of sensing technologies. Creating the world’s best products means solving some of the most challenging and unique design problems. Please come join us!
You will utilize your expertise in Finite Element Analysis (FEA) to solve engineering problems and discover creative solutions in order to enable robust and reliable sensor technologies. You will perform simulations that will be used to assess performance, design sensitivity, root-cause failure, reliability and much more. As an FEA engineer you will help address engineering challenges with a problem-solving, design-driven mindset to accelerate technology development and deliver world class products. This includes building FEA models, performing model validation and using FEA to provide critical design inputs to ensure performance and reliability goals are met. Simulation is a critical part of the design process and you will be working closely with product design partners, providing critical insights from simulation to ensure designs meet requirements. This position offers a technically challenging and rewarding opportunity to influence design and create real impact on our sensing technology portfolio.
Minimum qualifications: BS and a minimum of 10 years relevant industry experience
Experience with Abaqus, ANSYS, COMSOL, or other FEA tools
Strong engineering fundamentals in solid mechanics
Preferred qualifications: M.S. degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Applied Mechanics, Structural Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field
In-depth knowledge of FEA and CFD theory, implementation and numerical methods
Experience solving non-linear solid mechanics problems (materials, contact, geometric)
Experience in simulation applied to high volume consumer electronic products and sensor technologies
Experience applying simulation to human anatomy and human-device interaction, including tissue mechanics, physiological responses and human variability, to drive product development and translate these factors into actionable product performance insights, requirements, and specifications.
Experience in additional analysis/simulation areas (biofluid, acoustics, fatigue, and optical biomechanics) and multi-physics simulations
Applied knowledge/experience with material testing & material model calibration
Modeling nonlinear materials such as soft adhesives, elastomers, and polymers
Proficient in Matlab, Python or other scripting language and experience with using AI tools
Knowledge of GD&T fundamentals
Experience in data and statistical analysis (Monte Carlo, DOE, statistical process control)
Team-oriented with excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to interact and collaborate with management, team members and external vendors to achieve project goals, and give positively to the engineering community

ABOUT THE ROLE

Quant Analysts build and improve the models that drive Base’s Trading & Risk platform - the system that spans our distributed fleet of batteries and the households we serve. You’ll own the price models that tell Base where value exists in wholesale markets like ERCOT and PJM, and the hedging strategy that turns that analysis into a plan for managing Base’s risk.

This is a mid-to-senior role that combines quantitative analysis, software engineering, and energy market expertise. Base has a price model for ERCOT that provides the foundation for future improvements. You’ll extend that work to PJM, sharpen how Base captures grid congestion, and use what you build to shape Base’s hedging strategy there.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Improve Base’s price distributions by capturing grid congestion effects, like midday price excursions regularly seen, that our current models miss

 - Build a price model for PJM, so Base can track risk and make hedging decisions there as well as it already does in ERCOT

 - Build a hedging strategy for PJM, using the models you build to decide what that strategy should be




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Energy markets and domain knowledge: you understand wholesale energy market operations like ERCOT, including real-time arbitrage, ancillary services, and capacity, along with unit commitment, economic dispatch, and production cost modeling

 - Coding and SQL: you build models in Python (or another language) and pull your own data with SQL, and you can work through a model independently

 - Statistics and machine learning: You understand the bias-variance tradeoff, train/validation/test evaluation, and loss functions for categorical and continuous targets, and you’re deeply familiar with at least one statistical subfield, like extreme value theory, information theory, or stochastic processes. You’ve deployed models to production with versioning and maintenance, scaled training beyond a single machine, and know Python, pandas, and visualization libraries well.

Base’s Risk & Trading team turns the grid-service capability of our distributed battery fleet into revenue. That means building and defending the models that decide which markets and products Base participates in, from real-time arbitrage to multi-year distribution deals. The team’s calls carry real weight — a mis-modeled coincident peak or an unvetted market opinion shows up directly in Base’s book. You’ll work alongside traders, market operations engineers, and policy leads who bring the same rigor to distribution-scale energy that a trading desk brings to wholesale power.

About the Team
DoorDash's MDX team sits within Machine Learning Platform and builds the shared foundation that ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo rely on to build and run ML-powered products. We work across the full ML lifecycle: feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, serving, and monitoring. Our mission is to increase the velocity and reliability of ML-driven business impact across the company. A central pillar of that work is agentic infrastructure. We are building systems that let agents accelerate and operate the ML workflow itself, including auto research, where agents explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and self-healing systems that detect, diagnose, and remediate failures in ML pipelines and production models with minimal human intervention.
About the Role
You will join a small, high-leverage team building the agentic layer of DoorDash's ML infrastructure. You'll design and build the systems that let agents accelerate how ML engineers across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo develop, ship, and operate models. That includes auto research systems that explore and iterate on modeling ideas, and agentic developer support that helps ML engineers move through training, evaluation, deployment, and debugging faster. You'll own well-scoped components end to end, from design through production, working across agent orchestration, tooling and integrations with our ML platform, evaluation of agent behavior, and observability. This role is ideal for an engineer with a strong backend foundation who is excited to apply AI agents to real engineering workflows, learns quickly, and wants to grow into technical leadership in a fast-moving area where model capabilities, tooling, and best practices change month to month.

Build agentic systems that increase the velocity of ML development across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo, helping ML engineers get from idea to production model faster.
Design and implement infrastructure that lets agents propose, run, and evaluate modeling experiments.

Partner closely with ML engineers, data scientists, and platform teams to understand where their time goes and turn those workflows into durable, reusable platform capabilities.
Grow quickly in a fast-moving area, with the chance to shape how agents are used to build and operate ML systems at a company of this scale.

title: Inventory Control Coordinator
description:
Job Description:
Why this Role Matters
The Inventory Control Coordinator at ITW in Paris, Kentucky plays a critical role in ensuring manufacturing operations have the tooling, materials, and non-inventory supplies needed to meet customer demand. You will leverage analytical thinking and 80/20 principles to optimize inventory levels, improve material availability, reduce stock-outs and excess inventory, and strengthen supplier performance. Success in this role means maintaining a reliable supply chain that supports operational efficiency, cost control, and continuous improvement.
What You Will Do
Analyze inventory levels and consumption patterns to ensure on-hand materials meet manufacturing requirements, including expedited and exceptional production needs as communicated.
Support root cause analysis initiatives by evaluating reports, identifying usage trends, monitoring consumption changes, and investigating unusual inventory patterns.
Manage the RFQ process for all non-inventory materials, tooling, and related supplies.
Place purchase orders and proactively follow up on open orders while ensuring compliance with established pricing, discounts, and purchasing terms.
Establish and maintain Kanban systems and visual min-max inventory controls to promote effective communication, reorder accuracy, and operational continuity during employee absences.
Purchase replacement tooling and machine components in accordance with established Kanban replenishment processes.
Prepare, assemble, and issue tooling kits to support efficient manufacturing machine setups.
Maintain inventory and purchasing systems to effectively communicate inventory status, usage, orders, pricing, delivery schedules, and deadlines with internal stakeholders and suppliers.
Procure materials and services from approved suppliers, communicate price changes, and expedite deliveries to support operational requirements.
Collaborate with suppliers to develop and maintain replenishment, restocking, and consignment inventory programs.
Negotiate credits, pricing adjustments, and delivery accommodations; communicate production schedule changes and secure supplier commitments to prevent shipment delays while processing purchase orders.
Maintain accurate purchasing documentation, including acknowledgments, amendments, and supply requisitions; review packing slips for accuracy, resolve discrepancies, and submit documentation to Accounts Payable to ensure timely supplier payments.
Assist with supplier scorecards and performance evaluations while supporting supplier consolidation, corrective actions, and continuous improvement initiatives.
Partner with Accounts Payable to investigate and resolve discrepancies involving packing slips, purchase orders, and supplier invoices.
Generate and analyze monthly spending reports, providing leadership with insights into purchasing trends and cost management opportunities.
Manage inventory levels and place orders for production and packaging supplies through the SAP system to ensure uninterrupted operations.
Develop and maintain min-max inventory strategies for production and packaging supplies to optimize stock levels and material availability.
Conduct routine cost analyses and sourcing reviews to identify savings opportunities, improve supplier performance, and support cost-effective purchasing decisions.
Additional duties as assigned.
What You Bring (Requirements)
High School Diploma or GED required; Bachelor’s degree preferred.
3+ years of purchasing, inventory control, buyer, MRO, or tooling analyst experience in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
Strong understanding of purchasing processes, inventory management, and supply chain principles.
Proficiency with SAP or similar ERP systems and Microsoft Office applications; CMMS experience (FIIX preferred).
Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and multitasking skills.
Ability to build effective relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders; maintenance parts knowledge preferred.
What’s In It for You
Join a collaborative manufacturing environment where your work directly impacts production performance and operational excellence. You will have opportunities to drive process improvements, influence inventory strategy, and partner with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Grounded in four data-driven Core Commitments, we aim to ensure all colleagues—regardless of segment, division, geography or title—experience what differentiates ITW as a great employer.

title: Videographer & Motion Editor
description:
Job Description:
Job Summary
This is a high-impact, technical role for a video and motion professional who takes pride in the craft of visual storytelling. You will be a driving force for ITW Welding's family of brands, primarily Miller and Hobart, turning brand strategies and creative briefs into authentic, genuine video content that honors our nearly 100-year legacy. You will bridge the gap between the gritty reality of the shop floor and the high-stakes precision of the corporate boardroom. You will be responsible for capturing our distinct brand voices with the same honesty found in the work itself, creating content that speaks with equal authority to the welding fabricator at the bench, the leaders in the boardroom, and the distribution partners who rely on our brand reputation to drive their sales. You are a "master of the craft" and hands-on creative partner who advises and influences the vision while executing the work with technical precision.
Responsibilities
Cinematic Execution & Technical Strategy
Serve as a primary cinematographer on set, managing composition, lighting, and sound while providing technical video expertise alongside our product experts to capture the authentic reality of the work.
Utilize our dedicated on-site studio, featuring integrated lighting solutions and professional-grade infrastructure, to execute high-polish studio shoots.
Act as a creative partner to internal marketing teams and external agencies to help define and refine the look and feel of our brands.
Audit and maintain our internal equipment identifying the glass, bodies, and lighting needed to meet the cinematic standards of a world-class brand.
Navigate complex industrial environments: utilizing professional lighting techniques to manage high-heat, high-scale manufacturing spaces with precision.
Translate strategic briefs into visual frameworks that keep our motion output steadfast, premium, and scalable.
End-to-End Production
Own the process from the first frame to the final export, moving seamlessly from high-heat industrial environments to the edit suite.
Execute expert-level color grading, pacing, and sound design to ensure every narrative is clear and every delivery is professional.
Balance "A-List" flagship productions with the development of high-quality templates for efficient, quick-turn projects.
Build and maintain a highly organized post-production system: ensuring technical consistency, file management (DAM), and scalable delivery workflows.
Collaborative Partnership
·You must be as comfortable managing a solo shoot as you are collaborating on a two-camera set or dividing post-production tasks.
·Act as a collaborative peer to our existing motion team members, providing mutual creative "pressure-testing" to ensure every frame meets the Miller standard.
·You must be comfortable working in the heat and sparks to catch the authentic moments that cannot be faked.
·Provide technical expertise and creative feedback to partner divisions, ensuring all work, internal or agency-led, lives up to our brand promises.
Qualifications
5+ years of experience in high-end video production and editing within an agency or in-house environment.
In-depth knowledge of the end-to-end video workflow, from storyboarding to pre-production lighting and final delivery.
Mastery of camera systems and professional lighting for industrial spaces.
Advanced proficiency in Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, and After Effects.
A formal degree in Film, Cinematography, Visual Communications, or a related field is preferred, but not required with a proven track record of impactful work.
Foundational knowledge of the welding process or prior experience shooting in industrial/manufacturing environments is a significant plus, but not a requirement.
A portfolio of work must be provided that showcases a versatile range of motion projects from social-first content to cinematic brand storytelling and national spots.
Location and Travel
This role is based at our headquarters in Appleton, Wisconsin, working out of our dedicated production studio.
Expect 20-30% travel for on-location production as project needs dictate.
Candidates must be able to move 25 lbs of gear and work safely around heavy machinery and industrial environments.

As an Embedded Software Engineer in the Future Forward organization, you will work at the forefront of innovation, rapid prototyping, and new product development. You’ll collaborate with talented cross-functional teams—including engineers, clinicians, and product managers—to advance Intuitive’s robotic surgical platform, driving the entire product lifecycle from concept to launch.

Design and develop robust embedded software to enable system infrastructure, including OS drivers, hardware interfaces, real-time data pipelines, inter-processor communication, error handling, and user/test applications.

Translate early requirements into prototype implementations to evaluate, iterate, and advance novel robotic systems.
Conduct rigorous unit testing to support system integration and ensure reliable, robust system operation.

Produce clear and compliant supporting documentation in alignment with Intuitive's development and quality guidelines.
Ensure all designs meet rigorous quality and safety standards per the Intuitive Quality Management System.
A minimum of 5 years of experience in developing and supporting embedded systems; or 3 years with a Master’s degree; or 1 year with a PhD.
Highly proficient in developing C/C++ embedded and real-time software for multi-core, multi-processor systems, especially on embedded Linux and QNX.
Demonstrated experience with board bring-up, device driver development, and integration of new hardware components.
Skilled in version control systems and collaborative development environments, supporting efficient, iterative improvement.
Familiarity with a wide range of communication protocols—including TCP/IP, CAN, I2C, SPI—and serialization standards such as protobuf.
Strong problem-solving skills and debugging capabilities for complex embedded software and electromechanical systems.
In-depth understanding of failure mode and risk analysis, with a track record in safety-critical, product-focused designs.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills for effective interaction across all organizational levels.
Demonstrates passion for innovation, continuous learning, and developing solutions that make a meaningful difference in patients’ lives.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Experience with robotics and embedded software for complex electro-mechanical systems.
Knowledgeable in Python or Matlab for automation, diagnostics, and testing.
Familiarity with FPGA development and interfaces.
Familiarity with CUDA programming and memory management concepts.
Cyber-security concepts such as secure boot, authentication and encryption.
Hands-on engineering experience with proven ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Experience in all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing.
Experience designing software products in a regulated industry or for mission critical applications; comfort with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations.

description:

As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.

We’re looking for a Software Engineer who is passionate about building a modern, scalable Data as a Service (DaaS) platform that powers Intuitive’s Digital products and supports over 2,000 engineers across the organization. In this role, you will own and evolve critical components of our real-time and micro-batch data pipelines that power product development, internal tools, and analytics.
Your work will focus on enabling high-throughput, low-latency data delivery through streaming pipelines, dynamic transformations, and APIs, driving discoverability, accessibility, and actionable insights. You will help define the architecture and engineering practices that support self-service analytics and operational decision-making on scale.
As a catalyst for change, you will be at the forefront of reimagining how engineering teams consume and interact with data. Long-term success in this role means building robust, efficient systems and replacing legacy processes with modern solutions that allow teams to move faster, with greater confidence and autonomy.
Responsibilities:
Design and build scalable, distributed Data as a Service that ingest, process, and serve data from robotics, manufacturing, engineering, and clinical sources in real time and batch modes.
Develop and maintain robust APIs, data services, and tooling to provide internal teams with secure, efficient, and intuitive access to high-quality data.
Partner with engineering, analytics, and business stakeholders to evolve data contracts and models that support emerging use cases and ensure semantic consistency.
Implement CI/CD practices for data services, including automated testing for data quality, service reliability, and schema evolution.
Championing a self-service data culture by building discoverable, well-documented data products and guiding teams toward empowered, autonomous data access.
Act as a technical leader within the data domain driving best practices, mentoring teammates, and continuously improving how data is produced, shared, and consumed across the organization.
Qualifications:
Key Skills & Experience:
Solid quantitative background in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Math, or 3+ years of hands-on experience in a technically demanding role.
Proficient in at least two major programming languages such as Python, Go, Scala, C++, or Java, with a strong understanding of software design and architecture.
Proven experience building data pipelines and working with distributed systems using technologies like Apache Spark, Kafka, Elasticsearch, Snowflake, and Airflow.
Strong collaborator who actively contributes to code reviews, system design discussions, sprint planning, and KPI evaluations to drive team excellence and technical quality.
Minimum a bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field.
Bonus Points:
Experience working on Data Platform or Infrastructure Engineering teams.
Hands-on experience with AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Kafka, Elasticsearch, Apache Airflow, Snowflake, and Terraform.
Familiarity with CI/CD best practices for DataOps and deployment automation.
About the Data Services Team:
We are a rapidly growing organization made up of Software and Data Engineers, with a strong DevOps culture, focused on building a next-generation Data as a Service (DaaS) platform. We are seeking a strong technical lead who is passionate about designing scalable, real-time data systems that deliver high-quality, trusted data across the company.
Our platform leverages technologies such as Apache Kafka for real-time data ingestion, Apache Flink for stream processing and transformation, Snowflake for scalable warehousing, and AWS as our cloud backbone. title: Sr. Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience

description:
Job Purpose
The Senior Manager, Procurement Risk & Resilience leads the North America Procurement risk management and resilience strategy and owns responsible sourcing compliance for the region. This role owns the frameworks, governance, tools and cross-functional routines used to identify, assess, prioritize, monitor and mitigate supplier, material, financial, operational, regulatory, geopolitical, quality and sustainability-related risks, while driving supplier compliance with applicable SEDEX requirements.
The position partners closely with Category Procurement, Business Units, Supply Chain, Operations, R&D, Finance, Legal, Food Safety & Quality and Sustainability teams to embed risk into category strategies, sourcing decisions and supplier relationship management. The role strengthens supply continuity, improves decision quality and supports uninterrupted delivery of the company strategic and growth objectives.
Job Description
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
1. Risk & Resilience Strategy and Operating Model
Own and annually refresh the North America Procurement Risk & Resilience roadmap and three-year strategic plan, aligned with business priorities and ambitious risk-reduction targets.
Define the procurement risk operating model, including risk appetite, governance routines, intake and prioritization, KPI tracking and leadership escalation pathways.
Build capability roadmaps covering future-state tools, process improvements, automation opportunities and data enhancements.
Continuously improve risk frameworks, methodologies and controls based on business needs, emerging threats and lessons learned.
2. Material, Supplier and Supply Continuity Risk
Own the Material Risk Assessment methodology and annual AROP cycle, including methodology refresh, category engagement, risk scoring, mitigation planning and progress tracking.
Identify and refine the variables used to measure risk so that the highest-priority materials, suppliers and exposures are targeted for mitigation.
Lead third-party risk management across strategic and critical suppliers, monitoring financial, operational, quality, regulatory, ESG, geographic and geopolitical risks.
Partner with category teams to develop and advance mitigation plans, including alternate sourcing, dual sourcing, contingency planning and other resilience solutions.
Develop procurement resilience playbooks, conduct scenario planning and disruption simulations, and support crisis response and business recovery during supply disruptions.
Maintain accurate material risk trackers and optimize their usability, data quality and relevance for decision-making and reporting.
3. Responsible sourcing
Own North America Procurement’s SEDEX compliance program, governance and annual priorities, aligned with global requirements and business needs.
Manage supplier registration, site association and required information in SEDEX, partnering with category teams and suppliers to address gaps and maintain accurate records.
Monitor supplier and site compliance, track completion against established requirements and follow up on overdue or incomplete actions.
Coordinate with Sustainability, category teams and suppliers on SEDEX related issues, escalations and remediation actions.
Maintain SEDEX compliance dashboards and reporting, providing leadership with visibility to coverage, gaps, progress and priority actions.
Develop guidance and training to support consistent SEDEX compliance across North America Procurement.
4. Risk Decision Support and Category Enablement
Serve as the primary Procurement Risk point of contact for North America category teams and emerging risk issues, coordinating rapid assessment, stakeholder alignment and response recommendations.
Build and maintain a catalog of tools, templates and risk profiles that enable category teams to incorporate risk into category strategies, sourcing strategies, supplier reviews, SRM activities and joint business plans.
Lead regular category risk reviews, provide ad hoc guidance and troubleshooting, and drive mitigation progress against established KPIs.
Assemble cross-functional teams and create situation-specific decision frameworks to prioritize and address complex or critical risk exposures.
5. Cross-Functional Governance and Business Partnership
Lead governance routines with Supply Chain, Operations, Food Safety & Quality, R&D, Finance, Legal, Sustainability and other partners, integrating cross-functional risks that may affect supply continuity.
Partner with Business Units to prioritize critical mitigation projects, align resources and ensure the risk agenda supports strategic business objectives.
Present risk exposure, mitigation progress and priority decisions through BU performance routines and to senior Procurement and business leadership.
Strengthen procurement governance controls, monitor remediation and corrective actions, ensure compliance with policies and regulatory requirements, and support internal and external audits.
6. Digital Risk Intelligence, Data and Reporting
Lead the implementation and continuous improvement of procurement risk technologies, predictive analytics and automated monitoring capabilities.
Integrate relevant internal and external intelligence sources into risk processes and decision-making.
Build executive-ready dashboards and reporting that provide visibility to material and supplier risk exposure, mitigation pipelines, priority projects and performance against targets.
Own country-of-origin mapping capability and governance, including data refresh cadence, data ownership, collection standards, system integration and cross-functional use cases.
7. Communication, Training and Adoption
Develop and maintain annual stakeholder communication and engagement plans, including North America and Global Procurement risk updates.
Maintain the Risk Hub on Proc Connect so current tools, templates, guidance and training materials are accessible and ready for use.
Develop and deliver training on material and supplier risk, and maintain playbooks, SOPs and best-practice documentation to standardize processes and enable scalable adoption.
Drive adoption of Procurement Risk tools, dashboards, templates and practices across North America Procurement and support future deployment of the methodology to other regions.
Required Qualifications
Education
Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain, Procurement, Sustainability, Engineering, Operational Excellence or a related field.
Experience
6-9 years of experience in Procurement, Supply Chain, Risk Management or a related business function.
Demonstrated experience leading supplier or material risk programs and applying third-party risk management frameworks.
Experience in CPG, food manufacturing or another regulated industry preferred.
Experience implementing or managing risk technology platforms and analytics solutions.
Technical Skills
Strong knowledge of supplier and material risk management, business continuity planning, SEDEX compliance, financial risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and crisis management.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability, with the ability to connect data, risk exposure and business impact.
Proficiency with analytics and visualization tools; experience with Power BI, Tableau or similar platforms preferred.
Understanding of AI-enabled monitoring, automation and emerging digital risk capabilities.
Leadership & Behavioral Competencies
Acts as Procurement’s risk subject-matter expert and trusted advisor.
Influences without authority and builds alignment across senior, cross-functional stakeholders.
Communicates complex risk topics clearly and leads executive communications during disruptions.
Demonstrates strong project management, organizational and stakeholder-management skills.

Brings curiosity, sound judgment, a continuous-improvement mindset and a willingness to challenge the status quo.

title: Critical Environment Technician
description:
Overview
As a Critical Environment Technician in Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) team, you will maintain the critical infrastructure that keeps our Datacenters up and running. This could be anything from coordinating with supplier/vendors, recognizing safe versus unsafe work environment, having a hands-on understanding of how critical environment equipment works, performing various types of maintenance, responding to onsite incidents while coordinating with other critical facilities professionals, and using telemetry and other platforms to monitor equipment performance and operations.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Technician, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role’s job duties.
Responsibilities
Critical Environment Culture
Understands, follows, and ensures safety and security requirements (e.g., job hazard assessments [JHAs], toolbox talks), and business processes and procedures are met, to properly perform work in a safe, quality, and reliable manner in accordance to applicable Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations, and Microsoft requirements. Recognizes safe versus unsafe working conditions and responds accordingly (e.g., stop/pause tasks, stand down vendors where necessary). Escalates immediately when unsafe working conditions are observed and promotes a safe working culture to empower less experienced team members. Participates in required meetings, trainings, and necessary handoffs. Assesses and identifies appropriate resources and equipment necessary to fully support environmental health and safety (EHS) objectives. Actively maintains safe working conditions at all times. Proactively ensures safety and security requirements are followed and met for the work of themselves and others.
Equipment and Systems Maintenance
Prepares and submits required reports (e.g., turnover, preventative maintenance [PM]) as assigned following preexisting scripts and templates, or using ad hoc methods required to support trending and analysis (e.g., Maintenance data, equipment trending data). Develops methods of operating procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and/or digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for devices and disciplines within their coverage and expertise to ensure safe and reliable execution. Documents completed work using approved tools and procedural templates for more experienced technician review. Completes and provides coaching to support less experienced technicians for mandatory, technical, and procedural training assignments. Analyzes findings from reports and documents observations.
Performs various types of maintenance (e.g., planned, predictive, corrective) and repairs following methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) for multiple disciplines and one or more types of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, cooling systems) with minimal supervision - in consideration of Task Hazard Analysis (THA), Method Statement of Work (MSOW), or varying permit requirements. Communicates and/or escalates maintenance activities per established process and procedure. Prioritizes maintenance activities as required and/or appropriate. Documents tasks or issues during maintenance activities within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Performs maintenance tasks and repairs that can be performed with minimal oversight. Follows recommended maintenance schedules. Oversees maintenance tasks within a single discipline or area of expertise. Maintains all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner and understands levels of risk (LORs) associated with varying types of maintenance with established mastery of maintaining systems of a specific discipline.
Provides necessary escort to third-party contractors, sub-contractors, vendors, and service providers on site based on the appropriate procedure levels of risk (LOR). Takes part in getting third-party work underway (e.g., making sure systems are properly energized/deenergized), ensuring the work is started and completed in a safe manner in accordance with standard practices, procedures, and Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) regulations. Ensures work performed by suppliers/vendors is performed to scope, all documentation is performed correctly, and escalates as appropriate. Recognizes circumstances when to stop supplier/vendor work to address potential and/or identified concerns. Coordinates per appropriate LOR applicable to preventative and/or corrective maintenance. Identifies and recommends procedure corrections if/when errors are detected or when appropriate. Coordinates and schedules supplier/vendor on-site activities. Reviews and completes appropriate work orders to support approval of vendor supplier field service reports or invoices.
Processes method statement of work (MSOW) documents. Coordinates activities and associated schedules with contractors. Performs inspections of equipment in a facility. Participates in testing and commissioning activities.
Documents issues found in troubleshooting process within appropriate systems per process and procedure as needed. Ensures equipment and system settings are consistent with established parameters and designs. Determines when troubleshooting efforts are deemed adequate and communicates or escalates to suppliers, engineers, or more experienced colleagues as needed. Has a hands-on understanding of how equipment works within disciplines they have been trained and how to troubleshoot to a subsystem level. Provides consultation to less experienced colleagues with troubleshooting systems and problems. May lead efforts to troubleshoot issues and identify root causes.
Equipment and Systems Operations
Works on advanced tasks (e.g., vendor contact, escalations) independently. Serves as a subject matter expert in critical environments-related systems within the data center, and advises less experienced colleagues on such topics. Possesses an understanding of and operates equipment and systems within a set discipline (e.g., electrical, mechanical, controls) with knowledge of the interactions between them and overall operation of a data center. Operates all systems and equipment in a safe and professional manner.
Inspects and supervises critical environment-related facility equipment (e.g., controls, heating, ventilation, and air conditioning [HVAC], mechanical systems), building, and grounds for unsafe or abnormal conditions to develop and analyze trends. Understands critical system alarms for single discipline(s) of equipment, their meanings, and engages with appropriate escalation processes or procedures. Recognizes circumstances where execution would be considered safe to proceed. Performs various inspections and validations of equipment performance. Monitors the performance from central monitoring locations (i.e., Facility Operations Centers) of maintenance and operations of equipment (e.g., electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) within the data center. Escalates per applicable policies and standards. Utilizes telemetry, control systems, and other platforms to monitor site status, analyze past and current events, as well as other processes, and can identify all alarms. Uses technical expertise, prior experience, and device analytics to recognize trends with equipment behavior and checks potential issues as they arise. Advises less experienced colleagues on issues found while monitoring applicable CE systems. Performs all monitoring equipment repair, replacement, and maintenance work, which meets or exceeds Microsoft Service Level Agreement (SLA) requirements.
Utilizes internal computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) to track all equipment assets and to complete work order requests for maintenance work. Tracks hours for performed tasks within applicable task management systems. Adds required data, documents, logs changes, and upkeeps procedures related to building management systems and reports. Properly signals spare equipment and parts utilization within maintenance work orders.
Safety and quickly responds to and leads an onsite incident response team for all abnormal conditions that impact operations, and coordinates with other critical facilities professionals to perform corrective repairs, without supervision. Gathers necessary information and creates incident timelines/data, root-cause analyses, and/or action items following an abnormal condition as required. Identifies and contacts/engages appropriate parties to mitigate incidents as they occur. Develops new or follows preexisting emergency operating procedures (EOPs), methods of procedure (MOPs), standard operating procedures (SOPs), and digital methods of operating procedures (DMOPs) in relation to incidents. Directly provides emergency monitoring response to irregular or malfunctioning conditions.
Physical Requirements
Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Occasional climbing of ladders. Frequent climbing of stairs and/or ramps. Prolonged standing. Occasional lifting 50lbs / 22.5kg. Occasional push or pull 50-75 lbs / 22.5-34kg. with assistive device. Normal visual acuity (near, far and peripheral with correction), defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria. Normal color vision for electrical work, defined via standard medical terms and applicable criteria.
Working Conditions
Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles: Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.
As indicated above, this role has a travel requirement of up to 25% which means you may be required to travel, from time to time, as part of this role.
As indicated above,   have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays.
Other
Embodies our  culture  and  values

High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent.
Background Check Requirements:
Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
Microsoft Cloud Background Check:  This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Associate's Degree or technical trade certification (e.g., military, trade school), or higher-equivalent education OR High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent AND 1+ year(s) technical services experience (e.g., high-availability assembly/manufacturing/critical infrastructure environments such as data centers, oil and gas refineries, hospitals, pharmaceutical) OR equivalent experience.
